Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test opens a 7z archive whose header itself is compressed and uses a non-default dictionary size. The constructor SevenZFile(File) delegates to readHeaders, which detects an encoded header (kEncodedHeader) and calls readEncodedHeader to decode it. readEncodedHeader sets up the decoding stack by iterating the “coders” and routing each through Coders.addDecoder, which selects the appropriate decoder based on the coder’s method ID.

In this path, the encoded header is compressed with LZMA2 and carries a dictionary size parameter in the coder’s properties. When Coders.addDecoder hands the stream to the LZMA2 decoder, that decoder parses the properties and configures its dictionary. For archives created with a 16 MB dictionary (as described in the bug report), the decoder rejects the dictionary as “too big” and throws an exception during header decoding. This exception propagates back through readEncodedHeader/readHeaders and causes the SevenZFile constructor to fail, which is exactly what the test exposes by simply trying to open COMPRESS-256.7z.

In short:
- SevenZFile.readHeaders detects an encoded header and invokes readEncodedHeader.
- readEncodedHeader builds the decoder stack and invokes Coders.addDecoder for the LZMA2 coder.
- The LZMA2 decoder misinterprets or artificially limits the allowed dictionary size and rejects 16 MB as “too big”.
- The exception aborts header parsing, making SevenZFile(File) fail to open the archive.

This matches the user-facing report “7z: 16 MB dictionary is too big.” The root cause is in the LZMA2 decoder’s handling of the coder properties (dictionary size): either an incorrect conversion of the property byte to the dictionary size or an unnecessarily low upper bound, causing valid 7z LZMA2 streams with 16 MB dictionaries (including compressed headers) to be rejected.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

To proceed, I will look up the implementation classes for the LZMA/LZMA2 decoder used by SevenZ to identify the methods that parse coder properties (dictionary size).
